text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - European Union (EU) External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek on Thursday warned Slovakia it must strengthen its democratic process, including adherence to the rule of law, if the country wants to be considered for EU expansion.
- But Hans van den Broek said there was no danger of the EU cancelling Slovakia's association agreement.
- The EU will temporarily introduce an 8.9 percent anti-dumping custom fee on imports of Slovak steel pipes produced by Zeleziarne Podbrezova.
- President Michal Kovac said he would accept the resignation of Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik but that he was waiting for the government's proposal on the minister's successor.
- The three parties in the social dialogue - the government, trade unions and the employers' association - have agreed to resume talks on introduction of the so-called 13th salary on June 9, 1997.
- Association of Investment Companies and Funds said it was working on the basis of a new law on collective investment.
- The financial markets on Thursday continued in insignificant trading resulting from liquidity shortage on both money and forex markets.

SME - President Kovac has rejected accusations that it was personal fued between him and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar that thwarted referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last weekend. Kovac said the feud was not between the two persons but that it was fight for democracy, legal state and human and citizen rights in Slovakia.

- The nine largest opposition parties have worked out a draft law on direct presidential elections. The opposition will call an extraordinary parliamentary session to discuss the law, and said it was ready to initiate another petition action to call a new referendum on direct presidential elections if parliament fails to approve the law.
PRAVDA - Opposition parties said they would initiate public protests all around Slovakia on June 3 to protest the alleged thwarting of the two referendums by the government.

PRACA - Confederation of Trade Uions (KOZ) said it was receiving negative signals from abroad over the failed referendums last weekend. KOZ President Ivan Saktor said the unions might organise a nation-wide protest strike if the government continues in its anti-democratic policy.
